title: A download workbook that a program never finishes is neither logged nor cut off when the program returns.
text: `rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream` says a workbook never finished is logged as an error naming its target when the request ends, and a download is cut off. A program that throws, meets a limit or is cancelled mid-download is cut off: `nvs_host`'s isolate `finish` aborts the request's body stream, and the server ends the response in an error frame (`crates/nvs-host/src/isolate.rs`, `nvs_runtime::stream::Emit::abort`). A program that returns normally with the workbook unfinished ends its body cleanly, because `Workbook` registers nothing that runs at the request's end: its `finished` flag is read only by its own members (`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Workbook.nvs`). The browser then saves a broken file and nothing is logged. Closing it needs the workbook to learn at the request's end that it was not finished, log the error, and abort the response body, which no Novis member can do today.
